prop:qiu-scope-separation.proof_tex:
Let \(C_Q\), \(D\), and \(R\) denote, respectively, the covariate block, binary treatment, and outcome in \(\mathrm{lem:qiu\text{-}external\text{-}ate\text{-}characterization}\).  Relabel the variables for the purpose of comparing signatures by
\[
T_0=C_Q,\qquad X=\{D\},\qquad Y=\{R\},\qquad
V=C_Q\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{D,R\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\), the two entries of the present observation map under (1) are
\[
\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)
=\bigl(P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0)\bigr)
=\bigl(P_M(C_Q,D,R\mid S=1),P_M(C_Q)\bigr).
\tag{2}
\]
The cited lemma states that Qiu et al. use a selected observational law together with an external unbiased covariate margin.  Thus (2) proves equality of the two data-slot patterns after relabeling.  It does not assert equality, inclusion, or even nonempty intersection of the two model classes.

We next verify the estimand map.  Suppose only for this calculation that \(R\) has a finite numeric state space and \(D\) is binary.  Every sum below is finite, so no integrability or limiting condition is needed.  The definitions of \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\) and \(\psi_{x,y}\) give, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)
&=E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1)]
  -E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0)]\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,
  P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,
  P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{1,r}(M)
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{0,r}(M).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Hence the finite table \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\), whose coordinatewise role is made explicit in \(\mathrm{def:full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\), determines \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)\) through the displayed linear map.

The converse to this last implication fails inside a strictly positive finite Markovian DAG subclass.  Consider the graph \(D\to R\) with \(S\) isolated, take \(X=\{D\}\), \(Y=\{R\}\), and let \(T_0=\varnothing\).  Let \(U_D\) and \(U_S\) be independent Bernoulli\((1/2)\) variables, and let \(U_R\) be independent of them and uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,12\}\).  In model \(M_j\), set
\[
D=U_D,\qquad S=U_S,
\qquad
R_1=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 3+6D\},
\qquad
R_2=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 4+6D\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Each model is finite and recursive.  Its exogenous variables are mutually independent, so it is Markovian and therefore semi-Markovian; its structural equations follow the displayed DAG.  Also \(P_{M_j}(S=1)=1/2>0\).  Independence of \(S\) from \((D,R_j)\) yields the selected cell tables
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
&(D,R_j)=(0,1)&(0,0)&(1,1)&(1,0)\\ \hline
j=1&1/8&3/8&3/8&1/8\\
j=2&1/6&1/3&5/12&1/12.
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Every cell in (5) is positive; in fact both models satisfy the selected-cell lower bound \(1/12\).  Thus the positivity assertion uses no boundary point.  Intervention replaces the equation \(D=U_D\) and leaves the equation for \(R_j\) unchanged, so (4) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc|c}
&P_{M_j}(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))
&P_{M_j}(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
&\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M_j)\\ \hline
j=1&3/12&9/12&6/12\\
j=2&4/12&10/12&6/12.
\end{array}
\tag{6}
\]
Both scalar effects equal \(1/2\), while \(\psi_{0,1}(M_1)=1/4\ne1/3=\psi_{0,1}(M_2)\).  Therefore the linear map in (3) is not injective even on the stated positive finite DAG subclass: identification of the scalar effect alone cannot decide every coordinate of \(\boldsymbol\psi\).

It remains to establish the two scope separations.  By \(\mathrm{lem:qiu\text{-}external\text{-}ate\text{-}characterization}\), Qiu et al.'s theorem assumes unconfoundedness, treatment overlap on the covariate support, and a pairwise distinguishability condition on specified classes of propensity, covariate--potential-outcome, and selection laws.  Its conclusion identifies the single scalar \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), not every cell \(\psi_{x,y}\) for arbitrary semi-Markovian \(\mathcal G\).  Equation (6) additionally shows why the scalar conclusion cannot be inverted into the full-table conclusion.  Thus the cited theorem does not subsume the present arbitrary-cell graph problem.

Conversely, \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) restricts the present class to finite-state recursive semi-Markovian models and imposes only the listed graph, selection, and selected-cell positivity conditions.  The cited lemma states both that Qiu et al.'s exposition includes continuous covariate--outcome laws with densities and that its identification criterion is indexed by separately specified probability classes.  Continuous-law examples are not members of the present finite-state class.  Moreover, a graph \(\mathcal G\) and the membership conditions in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) do not supply a chosen triple of probability classes or assert Qiu et al.'s pairwise distinguishability condition.  Hence the present graph class does not subsume the cited setup.  Together with (2), (3), and (6), these observations prove precisely an input-shape and estimand-map analogy, the failure of the reverse estimand map, and non-subsumption in both directions, without claiming a literal model-class intersection.

snapshot.stmt: Qiu et al.'s external-data theorem and the present decision problem are analogues at the level of data slots and estimand mapping; no literal intersection of their model classes is asserted. After relabeling their covariate block as \(T_0\), binary treatment as \(X\), outcome as \(Y\), and observed substantive tuple as \(V\), their selected observational law and external unbiased covariate margin have the same slot pattern \(P(V\mid S=1),P(T_0)\). In any finite specialization with binary \(X\) and numeric \(Y\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\) is a finite linear contrast of the cells \(\psi_{x,y}\), so \(\boldsymbol\psi\) determines \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), whereas the converse fails even for strictly positive finite Markovian DAG models. Qiu et al.'s cited theorem is conditional on unconfoundedness, treatment overlap, and specified probability classes and concludes identification of the scalar \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), not arbitrary cells \(\psi_{x,y}\) on an arbitrary semi-Markovian \(\mathcal G\). Conversely, the present finite-state graph class neither contains their continuous-law examples nor, from \(\mathcal G\) alone, imposes their probability-class restrictions. Therefore neither theorem subsumes the other.

defs.def:full-kernel-collection: Run \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}(\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\) separately for every \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\), in the fixed lexicographic order. If every run returns \(F_{x,y}\), collect the results as \(\mathbf F=(F_{x,y}:(x,y)\in\mathcal I)^{\mathsf T}\), with coordinates indexed against the target table \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\). If any run returns \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), report the set of failed cells and do not form \(\mathbf F\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)=\{M:\text{ \(M\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}state}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}semi\text{-}markovian}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}selection}\), and \(q_S^M(v)\ge\epsilon\) for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\)}\}.\]

assumptions.ass:finite-state: Every substantive variable has a known finite state space and \(S\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:semi-markovian: \(M\) is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(\mathcal G\).
assumptions.ass:selected-epsilon: The model-induced selected cells satisfy \(q_S^M(v)\ge\epsilon\) for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\).

prop:boundary-reductions.proof_tex:
Fix \(\epsilon>0\), an input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), a model \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and a cell \((x,y)\).  By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\),
\[
q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1),\qquad q_0(t)=P_M(T_0=t).
\]
Moreover, Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}input\text{-}image}\) give \(P_M(S=1)>0\) and \(q_S(v)\geq\epsilon>0\) for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\).  Hence
\[
P_M(V=v)\ \geq\ P_M(V=v,S=1)
=P_M(S=1)q_S(v)
\geq P_M(S=1)\epsilon>0. \tag{1}
\]
Thus the full population law is strictly positive at every substantive cell.  In particular, every marginal of that law on a conditioning cell is positive.

Suppose first that \(T_0=V\).  The population-initialization clause of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) puts, for each \(v\in\mathcal X_V\), the key
\[
 (V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)
\]
in the initial state with annotation
\[
q_0(v)=P_M(T_0=v)=P_M(V=v). \tag{2}
\]
Consider any finite, cellwise derivation of \(P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) from \(P_M(V)\) using ordinary finite probability manipulations and the three rules of do-calculus.  Every initial scalar in this derivation is present by (2).  We prove inductively over the derivation that the scalar key produced at each step becomes present in the saturation state.  For the induction step, all of the finitely many input keys are present.  If the step is a probability manipulation, the corresponding marginalization, conditioning, or chain instance is one of the complete scalar moves in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\); a division occurs only at a positive conditioning cell, as required there.  Positivity for conditionals formed directly from the observational law follows from (1), and positivity of any other conditioning cell used is part of the legality of the stipulated cellwise derivation.  If the step is do-calculus, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}graphical\text{-}fixing\text{-}moves}\) give the corresponding population-tagged move and the equality of its input and output kernels.

In either case, the move instance lies in the finite universe \(\mathscr U\), its complete input-key set is present, and its graphical and denominator premises hold.  If its output is not already present, it remains enabled because Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) only adds keys.  It cannot be postponed forever: each move chosen before it adds a previously absent key, while Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}extid\text{-}sound\text{-}termination}\) bounds the total number of present keys by \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\).  Equivalently, a terminal state omitting that output would contradict the rule that failure occurs only when no enabled instance has an absent output.  This proves the induction.

Therefore the target key \((Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast)\) becomes present.  It is checked before the next transition and its annotation is returned.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\) identifies that annotation, simultaneously for every model in the exact fiber, with
\[
k^M_{(Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop})}(y\mid x,\ast)
=P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
=\psi_{x,y}(M). \tag{3}
\]
The stored expression belongs to \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) by Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}arithmetic\text{-}language}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinary\text{-}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}completeness}\) supplies such a finite ordinary derivation whenever the target cell is identifiable from the full observational law, proving the first reduction.

Suppose next that \(\mathcal G\) entails \(S\perp\!\!\!\perp V\).  The selected initialization provides
\[
(V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{sel},v,\ast,\ast)
\quad\text{with annotation}\quad q_S(v)
\]
for every \(v\).  With \(A=V\) and \(B=C=\varnothing\), the graphical predicate for population storage in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) is exactly \(V\perp\!\!\!\perp S\).  Hence saturation makes the corresponding population key present, unless it is already present from population initialization, and preserves its annotation.  The storage invariant then yields
\[
q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1)=P_M(V=v), \tag{4}
\]
where conditioning is defined because \(P_M(S=1)>0\).  Thus the same full-population scalar keys are available with the claimed annotations.

Now let \(T_0=\varnothing\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\), the unique trivial margin contributes no scalar key.  A margin-extension instance in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) requires a nonempty population-margin input key, so no such instance is admissible.  To prove the asserted exact closure, inspect a transition according to its source tag.  Initially every present key is selected-tagged.  Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}graphical\text{-}fixing\text{-}moves}\) preserve the source tag.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) says that the only source-changing moves are margin extension and population storage.  The first is unavailable, while the second maps
\[
(A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)
\longmapsto
(A,B,C,\mathrm{pop},a,b,c) \tag{5}
\]
with unchanged annotation exactly when
\[
A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C
\quad\text{in }G_{\overline B}. \tag{6}
\]
Induction on the number of transitions therefore shows that every selected key belongs to the closure of the selected initialization under selected probability and graphical-fixing moves, and every population key is either an output (5) satisfying (6) or is obtained from such outputs by population probability and graphical-fixing moves.  Conversely, any absent output in these two closures whose complete inputs are present remains enabled; finiteness and the same no-permanent-postponement argument used above show that saturation adds it before terminating.  Hence there are no fewer and no additional keys than the stated closure.  Setting \(B=C=\varnothing\) in (6) gives precisely unconditional selection independence.

Finally, suppose margin extension reconstructs every cell of the full population law.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}margin\text{-}extension}\) gives, at every reconstructed cell \((t,z)\),
\[
P_M(T_0=t,Z=z)
=P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)q_0(t), \tag{7}
\]
and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\) says that the margin-transition annotation is exactly the right-hand side of (7).  Taking \(Z=V\setminus T_0\), or composing the reconstructed population blocks by the probability moves, therefore makes every key
\[
(V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)
\]
present with annotation \(P_M(V=v)\).  The finite-derivation replay leading to (3) now applies verbatim.  In particular, under an adjustment criterion with adjustment block \(L\), the ordinary derivation returns the standard functional
\[
P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal X_L}P_M(Y=y\mid X=x,L=\ell)P_M(L=\ell), \tag{8}
\]
and under the corresponding front-door criterion with mediating block \(D\), it returns
\[
P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
=\sum_{d\in\mathcal X_D}P_M(D=d\mid X=x)
  \sum_{x'\in\mathcal X_X}P_M(Y=y\mid D=d,X=x')P_M(X=x'). \tag{9}
\]
The graphical criteria are exactly the premises under which the usual do-calculus derivations of (8) and (9) are legal; Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) validates each graphical equality, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\) realizes their finite sums, products, and positive divisions.  Thus these are particular instances of the already proved replay argument, not additional identification assumptions.

Apply (3) separately to every successful \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\); each such returned coordinate equals the corresponding coordinate of \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\) throughout the exact fiber.  If every cell run succeeds, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\) forms \(\mathbf F\) and places those coordinates in the same fixed order as \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\).  Therefore, on the exact fiber,
\[
\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)
=\bigl(F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\bigr)^{\mathsf T}
=\bigl(\psi_{x,y}(M):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\bigr)^{\mathsf T}
=\boldsymbol\psi(M).
\]
When some cell run fails, that definition does not form \(\mathbf F\), but the coordinatewise equality just proved remains valid for every returned cell.  This proves all four reductions and the final coordinatewise collection claim.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(\epsilon>0\), \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and a cell \((x,y)\). The exact transition system has four audited reductions. If \(T_0=V\), initialization stores every scalar cell \(q_0(v)=P_M(V=v)\) at \((V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)\); consequently, whenever \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from the full population law by a finite sequence of ordinary do-calculus and probability moves, the saturation returns a valid arithmetic functional for that cell. If \(\mathcal G\) entails \(S\perp\!\!\!\perp V\), population storage inserts the same full-population scalar keys with annotations \(q_S(v)=P_M(V=v)\). If \(T_0=\varnothing\), the external-margin law is trivial, its scalar unit creates no key, and no margin-extension instance is admissible. The resulting boundary is the selected-source scalar closure augmented by exactly the population kernels inserted from a selected key \((A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\), together with their consequences under the unchanged population graphical-fixing and probability moves; at \(B=C=\varnothing\), the storage predicate is unconditional selection independence. Whenever margin extension reconstructs every cell of \(P_M(V)\), the same qualified full-law conclusion holds; in particular, under the corresponding adjustment or front-door graphical criterion, the saturation returns a valid expression equal to the standard adjustment or front-door functional. Collecting all successful \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\) gives the corresponding identified coordinates of the full conditional-kernel table on the exact fiber.

defs.def:compatible-input-image: \[\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)=\{\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M):M\in\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)\}.\] This is exactly the image of the positive graph-compatible model class; membership is not defined through existence of a separating pair.
defs.def:exact-observed-fiber: For \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), \[\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)=\{M\in\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G):\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)=(q_S,q_0)\}.\]
defs.def:extid-state-machine: On input \((\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\), \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) initializes, for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\), the scalar key \((V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{sel},v,\ast,\ast)\) with annotation \(q_S(v)\) and provenance \(\mathrm{init}_S\). When \(T_0\ne\varnothing\), it also initializes, for every \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\), \((T_0,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},t,\ast,\ast)\) with \(q_0(t)\) and provenance \(\mathrm{init}_0\); when \(T_0=V\), these are exactly all cells of the full population law. When \(T_0=\varnothing\), \(q_0\) is the unique trivial law, its scalar unit creates no key, and no margin-extension instance is admissible because its required nonempty population-margin input key is absent. Population storage remains admissible whenever its unchanged predicate \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\) holds, including the corresponding unconditional selection-independence predicate when \(B=C=\varnothing\). At each state the scalar target key \((Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast)\) is checked first. Otherwise the procedure scans \(\mathscr U\) in the order \(\mathrm{popstore},\mathrm{margin},\mathrm{popfix}_1,\mathrm{popfix}_2,\mathrm{popfix}_3,\mathrm{selfix}_1,\mathrm{selfix}_2,\mathrm{selfix}_3,\mathrm{marginal},\mathrm{condition},\mathrm{chain}\), then lexicographically, and takes the first instance whose exact premises hold, whose complete finite input-key set is contained in \(K_\sigma\), and whose one output scalar key is absent. It adds that output key, stores the displayed scalar arithmetic annotation and backpointer, and preserves all old entries. A present output is a duplicate and is skipped without overwrite. The target annotation is returned as \(F_{x,y}\); if no enabled instance has an absent output, \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) is returned. Formula spelling and derivation length never affect key identity or priority.
defs.def:graphical-fixing-moves: Write \(G_{\overline B}\) for \(\mathcal G\) with arrows into \(B\) removed, \(G_{\overline B,\underline H}\) also with arrows out of \(H\) removed, and \(H_s(C)=H\setminus\operatorname{An}_{G_{\overline B}}(C\cup S_s)\). For \(s\in\{\mathrm{pop},\mathrm{sel}\}\), each scalar transition has arity one, retains its source tag, copies the input annotation, and introduces no denominator. Rule \(1\) maps \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\leftrightarrow(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B}\). Rule \(2\) maps \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\leftrightarrow(A,B\cup H,C,s,a,(b,h),c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B,\underline H}\). Rule \(3\) maps \((A,B\cup H,C,s,a,(b,h),c)\leftrightarrow(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B,\overline{H_s(C)}}\). Each displayed reverse and each cell \((a,b,c,h)\) is a separate canonical move instance. The \(\mathrm{popfix}_r\) tags have \(s=\mathrm{pop}\), and \(\mathrm{selfix}_r\) have \(s=\mathrm{sel}\), so the latter condition every separation test on \(S=1\). Disjointness of \(A,B,C,H\), nonemptiness of \(A,H\), membership of both scalar keys in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and definition of the displayed input cell are mandatory.
defs.def:probability-moves: For every source tag \(s\), intervention block \(B\), conditioning block \(C\), disjoint nonempty blocks \(A,H\), and fixed output cell, the following are the complete scalar probability-calculus moves. Marginalization requires the \(\lvert\mathcal X_H\rvert\) input keys \(\{(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c):h\in\mathcal X_H\}\), outputs \((A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\), and stores \(E_{\mathrm{out}}=\sum_hE_\sigma(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c)\); it introduces no denominator. Conditioning requires all \(\lvert\mathcal X_A\rvert\) keys \(\{(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a',h),b,c):a'\in\mathcal X_A\}\), outputs \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\), and stores the annotation at \((a,h)\) divided by the sum over \(a'\); it is admissible exactly when that denominator is positive. Chain composition has arity two: inputs \((A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) and \((H,B,C\cup A,s,h,b,(c,a))\), output \((A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c)\), and stored product of the two scalar annotations. The symmetric chain instance interchanges \(A,H\); only the lexicographically first representation of an identical output scalar key is eligible. Each required input and output belongs to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and each move instance records its complete finite input-key set.
defs.def:source-bridge-moves: Margin extension has arity two at each cell. For nonempty \(Z\subseteq V\setminus T_0\), fixed \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\), and fixed \(z\in\mathcal X_Z\), its only input keys are \((Z,\varnothing,T_0,\mathrm{sel},z,\ast,t)\) and \((T_0,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},t,\ast,\ast)\). If \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid T_0\) in \(\mathcal G\) and the selected conditional cell is defined, the output is \((T_0\cup Z,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},(t,z),\ast,\ast)\), with annotation equal to the product of the two input annotations. Population storage has arity one at each \((a,b,c)\): input \((A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)\), output \((A,B,C,\mathrm{pop},a,b,c)\), and unchanged annotation when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\). Every conditioning cell used by an input must have positive probability. These are the only source-changing moves, and every output belongs to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\).

prop:source-specific-delta-method.proof_tex:
Put \(p=(q_S,q_0)\) and \(\widehat p=(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0)\).  First, the soundness conclusion for the successful EXT-ID runs gives, cell by cell,
\[
F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)
\qquad ((x,y)\in\mathcal I)
\]
for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\).  The definition of the lexicographically ordered full-kernel collection therefore gives
\[
\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\boldsymbol\psi(M).
\]
This step uses the EXT-ID soundness theorem; it does not define the causal target to equal the observed-law functional.

We next derive the stochastic expansion.  The empirical residuals are in the declared multinomial tangent spaces because
\[
\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}(e_o-q_S)=0,
\qquad
\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}(e_o-q_0)=0.
\]
Consequently the source derivatives in the influence-function definition may be applied to them.  Linearity gives the exact identities
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_S\mathbf F[\widehat q_S-q_S]
&=\frac1{n_S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_S}
D_S\mathbf F[e_{O_i^S}-q_S]
=\frac1{n_S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_S}\phi_S(O_i^S),\\
D_0\mathbf F[\widehat q_0-q_0]
&=\frac1{n_0}\sum_{j=1}^{n_0}
D_0\mathbf F[e_{O_j^0}-q_0]
=\frac1{n_0}\sum_{j=1}^{n_0}\phi_0(O_j^0).
\end{aligned}
\]
For a probability vector \(q\) on a finite set and its empirical table \(\widehat q_N\), direct calculation yields
\[
\mathbb E_q\|\widehat q_N-q\|_2^2
=\frac1N\sum_o q(o)\{1-q(o)\}
=\frac{1-\sum_o q(o)^2}{N}\le \frac1N.
\]
The inequality
\[
\mathbf 1\{\|R\|_2>u\}\le \|R\|_2^2/u^2
\]
then shows that \(\widehat q_S-q_S=O_P(n_S^{-1/2})\) and \(\widehat q_0-q_0=O_P(n_0^{-1/2})\).  The sample-share assumption implies that \(n_S\), \(n_0\), and \(n\) have the same order.

By differentiability of the returned finite-dimensional map at \(p\),
\[
\mathbf F(\widehat p)-\mathbf F(p)
=D_S\mathbf F[\widehat q_S-q_S]
+D_0\mathbf F[\widehat q_0-q_0]+r_n,
\qquad
\frac{\|r_n\|_2}{\|\widehat q_S-q_S\|_2+\|\widehat q_0-q_0\|_2}
\xrightarrow{P}0.
\]
Every population denominator is strictly positive by the positive-denominator assumption.  Because there are finitely many continuous denominators, there is a neighborhood of \(p\) on which they remain positive.  The empirical tables enter this neighborhood with probability tending to one by the preceding bound.  Thus the zero fallback in the totalized plug-in definition is used with probability tending to zero and does not alter the displayed first-order expansion.  Hence \(r_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), and multiplication by \(\sqrt n\) gives the asserted asymptotic linear representation.

It remains to identify its limit.  The influence vectors are centered:
\[
\mathbb E_{q_S}\phi_S(O^S)
=D_S\mathbf F\!\left[\sum_o q_S(o)(e_o-q_S)\right]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_{q_0}\phi_0(O^0)=0.
\]
Form one triangular row from the mutually independent vectors
\[
R_{n,i}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_S}\phi_S(O_i^S),
\quad 1\le i\le n_S,
\qquad
R_{n,n_S+j}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_0}\phi_0(O_j^0),
\quad 1\le j\le n_0.
\]
The state spaces are finite, so both influence vectors are bounded.  Since \(\sqrt n/n_S=O(n^{-1/2})\) and \(\sqrt n/n_0=O(n^{-1/2})\), for every \(u>0\) all summands have norm at most \(u\) for sufficiently large \(n\); the Lindeberg sum is therefore eventually zero.  Independence of the two samples and the sample-share limit give
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\operatorname{Cov}(R_{n,\ell})
=\frac n{n_S}\operatorname{Var}_{q_S}(\phi_S)
+\frac n{n_0}\operatorname{Var}_{q_0}(\phi_0)
\longrightarrow
\lambda^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q_S}(\phi_S)
+(1-\lambda)^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q_0}(\phi_0)
=\Sigma.
\]
The cited multivariate Lindeberg--Feller theorem now yields convergence of the linear term to \(N(0,\Sigma)\).  The cited asymptotic-equivalence theorem absorbs the \(o_P(1)\) remainder.  This proves both the displayed expansion and the claimed limit law.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(\epsilon>0\), \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), and \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\). If every cell run over \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\) returns a differentiable \(F_{x,y}\), then \(\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\boldsymbol\psi(M)\), and the saturated two-source plug-in estimator obeys \[\sqrt n\{\widehat{\mathbf F}-\mathbf F\}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_S}\phi_S(O_i^S)+\frac{\sqrt n}{n_0}\sum_{j=1}^{n_0}\phi_0(O_j^0)+o_P(1)\rightsquigarrow N(0,\Sigma).\]

defs.def:arithmetic-language: For a fixed input \((q_S,q_0)\), \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) is the smallest class of scalar expressions containing every cell of \(q_S\) and \(q_0\) and closed under finite addition, multiplication, and division by an expression whose value at that input is positive. A successful cell run returns one \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\); causal validity is asserted only when \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\).

prop:uniform-bonferroni-coverage.proof_tex:
Fix the returned vector expression \(\mathbf F\) from the success branch in the proposed statement, write \(p=(q_S,q_0)\), and write \(P_p\) for the two-source sampling law at \(p\).  The finite arithmetic-language definition expresses every coordinate of \(\mathbf F\) as a rational function of finitely many probability cells.  On \(\mathcal K\), every denominator is bounded below by a common number \(\gamma>0\).  Since \(\mathcal K\) is compact and there are finitely many denominators, continuity supplies \(\rho>0\) such that every denominator is at least \(\gamma/2\) whenever a table pair lies within Euclidean distance \(\rho\) of \(\mathcal K\).  On this neighborhood \(\mathbf F\) is twice continuously differentiable, and compactness bounds its first and second derivatives by finite constants.  By continuity of the covariance formula and the assumed uniform positive lower bound on every coordinate variance, \(\rho\) may be decreased so that, once \(n_S/n\) is sufficiently close to \(\lambda\), every plug-in diagonal variance is positive throughout the same neighborhood.

Let \(\mathcal E_n(p)\) be the event
\[
\|\widehat q_S-q_S\|_2+\|\widehat q_0-q_0\|_2<\rho.
\]
The exact multinomial second-moment calculation from the source-specific proposition and the elementary inequality \(\mathbf 1\{R>u\}\le R^2/u^2\) imply
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal K}P_p\{\mathcal E_n(p)^c\}
\le \frac{4}{\rho^2n_S}+\frac{4}{\rho^2n_0}
\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the fallback branches in the corrected plug-in, covariance, and confidence-region definitions have probability tending to zero uniformly over \(\mathcal K\).  On \(\mathcal E_n(p)\), the integral Taylor remainder and the uniform second-derivative bound give a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(p\in\mathcal K\), such that
\[
\left\|\mathbf F(\widehat p)-\mathbf F(p)
-D_S\mathbf F_p[\widehat q_S-q_S]
-D_0\mathbf F_p[\widehat q_0-q_0]\right\|_2
\le C\bigl(\|\widehat q_S-q_S\|_2+\|\widehat q_0-q_0\|_2\bigr)^2.
\]
Because the expectation of the squared quantity in parentheses is \(O(n^{-1})\) uniformly and \(n_S/n\to\lambda\in(0,1)\), another application of the same elementary probability bound shows that the Taylor remainder is \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).

We next verify covariance consistency rather than assuming it.  For \(p\in\mathcal K\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_{S,p}(o)&=D_S\mathbf F_p[e_o-q_S],
&V_S(p)&=\sum_{o\in\mathcal X_V}q_S(o)\phi_{S,p}(o)\phi_{S,p}(o)^{\mathsf T},\\
\phi_{0,p}(o)&=D_0\mathbf F_p[e_o-q_0],
&V_0(p)&=\sum_{o\in\mathcal X_{T_0}}q_0(o)\phi_{0,p}(o)\phi_{0,p}(o)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The centering calculation in the preceding proposition shows that these second moments are the corresponding variances.  Hence
\[
\Sigma(p)=\lambda^{-1}V_S(p)+(1-\lambda)^{-1}V_0(p).
\]
By the corrected definition of the empirical covariance, on \(\mathcal E_n(p)\) it is the same finite formula with \(p\) replaced by \(\widehat p\) and \(\lambda\) replaced by \(n_S/n\).  That formula is continuous on the common neighborhood and uniformly continuous on its compact closure.  The uniform concentration bound and \(n_S/n\to\lambda\) therefore imply, for every \(\delta>0\),
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal K}P_p\{\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma(p)\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\delta\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The zero-matrix fallback contributes only on \(\mathcal E_n(p)^c\), whose probability has already been bounded uniformly.  This proves the first conclusion of the proposed statement.

For coverage, it remains to establish a uniform, rather than merely pointwise, central limit argument.  Suppose to the contrary that the asserted lower bound fails.  Then there are a number \(\eta>0\), a subsequence of sample sizes (not relabeled), points \(p_n=(q_{S,n},q_{0,n})\in\mathcal K\), and models \(M_n\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_{S,n},q_{0,n})\) such that the coverage probability is below \(1-\alpha-\eta\).  Compactness permits passage to a further subsequence for which \(p_n\to p_\star\in\mathcal K\).

For this triangular sequence define the independent centered summands
\[
R_{n,i}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_S}\phi_{S,p_n}(O_i^S),
\qquad
R_{n,n_S+j}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_0}\phi_{0,p_n}(O_j^0).
\]
Uniform boundedness of the first derivatives on the common neighborhood and finiteness of both state spaces imply
\[
\max_{1\le \ell\le n}\|R_{n,\ell}\|_2=O(n^{-1/2}),
\]
so the Lindeberg condition holds.  Continuity of \(V_S\) and \(V_0\), together with the sample-share limit, gives
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\operatorname{Cov}_{p_n}(R_{n,\ell})
=\frac n{n_S}V_S(p_n)+\frac n{n_0}V_0(p_n)
\longrightarrow\Sigma(p_\star).
\]
The cited Lindeberg--Feller theorem, the uniform Taylor expansion, and the cited asymptotic-equivalence result yield
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat{\mathbf F}-\mathbf F(p_n)\}
\rightsquigarrow N\{0,\Sigma(p_\star)\}.
\]
Uniform covariance consistency also gives \(\widehat\Sigma\xrightarrow{P}\Sigma(p_\star)\) along this sequence.  The coordinatewise variance assumption supplies a common \(\underline\sigma>0\) with \(\Sigma_{kk}(p)\ge\underline\sigma\) for every \(p\in\mathcal K\) and every \(k\).  Define the studentized vector coordinatewise by
\[
T_{n,k}=\frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat{\mathbf F}_k-\mathbf F_k(p_n)\}}{\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{kk}}}
\]
when all diagonal entries of \(\widehat\Sigma\) are positive, and set \(T_n=0\) otherwise.  On the latter event the corrected confidence region is \(\mathbb R^d\), and \(0\) belongs to the Bonferroni rectangle, so
\[
\{\mathbf F(p_n)\in\widehat C_{1-\alpha}\}
=\left\{\max_{1\le k\le d}|T_{n,k}|\le c_{1-\alpha}\right\}
\]
holds on both branches.  Define
\[
D_\star=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\Sigma_{11}(p_\star),\ldots,\Sigma_{dd}(p_\star)\bigr).
\]
The cited joint-convergence and continuous-mapping results therefore show that the studentized vector converges to
\[
Z_\star\sim N(0,R_\star),
\qquad
R_\star=D_\star^{-1/2}\Sigma(p_\star)D_\star^{-1/2},
\]
whose every marginal is standard normal.

Let \(B=\{z:\max_{1\le k\le d}|z_k|\le c_{1-\alpha}\}\).  Its boundary is contained in the finite union of hyperplanes \(\{z:z_k=\pm c_{1-\alpha}\}\).  Each has \(Z_\star\)-probability zero because the corresponding marginal is a continuous standard normal law.  The continuity-set clause of the cited portmanteau lemma thus gives
\[
P_{p_n}\{\mathbf F(p_n)\in\widehat C_{1-\alpha}\}
\longrightarrow P\{Z_\star\in B\}.
\]
Finally, by the union bound and the definition \(c_{1-\alpha}=\Phi^{-1}\{1-\alpha/(2d)\}\),
\[
P\{Z_\star\notin B\}
\le\sum_{k=1}^{d}P\{|Z_{\star,k}|>c_{1-\alpha}\}
=d\,\frac{\alpha}{d}=\alpha.
\]
Thus the limiting coverage along the allegedly bad subsequence is at least \(1-\alpha\), a contradiction.

For every \(n\), the EXT-ID soundness conclusion in the source-specific proposition gives \(\boldsymbol\psi(M_n)=\mathbf F(p_n)\).  The coverage event therefore does not vary with the choice of \(M_n\) inside its exact observed-data fiber.  Taking the infimum over such models and reversing the contradiction argument proves
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal K}
\inf_{M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)}
P_{q_S,q_0}\{\boldsymbol\psi(M)\in\widehat C_{1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]

prose_overlay.tldr: The achieved headline is a graph-level necessity result on the terminal-unconfounded selection subclass, not universal completeness of EXT-ID. If a causal cell is not identifiable from a strictly positive full observational law on the substantive ADMG \(\mathcal G[V]\), Kivva et al.'s positive ordinary-ID specialization supplies two positive finite models with the same \(P(V)\) and different intervention cells. Extending both by any common strictly positive terminal selection kernel preserves the same normalized selected law \(q_S=P(V\mid S=1)\), every external margin \(q_0=P(T_0)\), and the causal disagreement in one exact \(\epsilon\)-positive fiber. Hence recovery from the two laws on this subclass requires ordinary positive-model identification. At \(T_0=V\), this converse combines with the boundary reduction to give an exact equivalence, and EXT-ID succeeds for every ordinarily identifiable positive-model cell. The general algebraic SCM class remains broader than the terminal-sink subclass; successful EXT-ID formulas are sound and the procedure terminates, but a bare EXT-ID failure is not a universal nonidentification certificate. The projective null-space theorem and canonical response-fiber characterization remain conditional and fixed-fiber supporting results.
prose_overlay.related_work: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim (2019, Definition 4, Algorithms 2--3, and Theorem 4) formulate the selected-conditional-plus-unbiased-margin problem and prove IDSB sound, while leaving completeness unresolved. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2021, Theorems 2--3 and Table 1) provide sound terminating do-search, but their negative-answer guarantee excludes unrestricted generalized identifiability, so it does not certify failure for the present source pair. Shpitser and Pearl (2006, Theorem 7) supply ordinary do-calculus completeness and the ordinary graph obstruction only; no global positivity claim is attributed to their hedge construction. Kivva et al. (2022, Definition 5 and Theorems 1--2), specialized to the singleton full-observational input, supply two positive finite substantive models with the same strictly positive \(P(V)\) and different target cells when ordinary positive-model identification fails. The present theorem's new step is to lift that pair through a common terminal-unconfounded selection kernel and prove exact equality of both observed sources. Qiu et al. (2026, Appendix B.2) study scalar ATE recovery from a selected observational law and an unbiased covariate margin under unconfoundedness, overlap, and probability-class restrictions. Their continuous-density exposition and probability-class theorem make it an input-shape and estimand analogue only; no literal finite-discrete class intersection is claimed. Richardson et al. inform successful fixing branches, Duarte et al. inform the finite response-fiber feasibility characterization, and Bhattacharya et al. inform supporting inference. Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser study a different systematic-selection likelihood. Li, Buchanan, and Cole provide the ACTG 320 applied benchmark, not evidence for the structural theorem.
prose_overlay.interpretation: On a terminal-unconfounded selection diagram, a strictly positive selection mechanism transforms the common substantive law by the same positive reweighting and normalization in both witness models. Because every external margin \(P(T_0)\) is already a marginal of that common substantive law, adding one such margin cannot distinguish the witnesses. Therefore two-law recovery on this subclass can occur only if the causal cell was already identifiable from \(P(V)\). When the margin is the full set \(T_0=V\), it directly reveals \(P(V)\), so the necessary condition becomes sufficient and EXT-ID replays ordinary identification. For an ACTG 320 audit using WIHS or CNICS margins, this gives a concrete negative diagnostic when the audited selection node is a terminal unconfounded sink and the substantive query fails ordinary positive-model ID; outside that graph subclass the theorem is not invoked.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The general finite selection-ADMG framework intentionally permits directed children of \(S\) and bidirected selection confounding. The graph-level transfer applies only when \(S\) is terminal and no bidirected edge is incident to it. It proves a necessary condition for recovery and the exact \(T_0=V\) equivalence, not completeness of EXT-ID on the broader class. The projective null-space theorem remains conditional on a chosen finite response representation and a separating query row; it does not extract such a representation from an arbitrary EXT-ID failure. The canonical response-fiber formula characterizes nonidentification at a fixed observed pair, but no implication from bare \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) to its feasibility has been proved. The parameterized three-node QE3/CAD audit has not been executed, and no universal margin-anchored hedge for every terminal failure is claimed. Presolve values such as \(19/36\) and the \(1/3\) versus \(2/3\) two-node pair remain diagnostics rather than proof premises.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The achieved tier is a scoped graph-level structural result: positive ordinary nonidentification transfers to exact two-law nonidentification for terminal selection sinks without incident bidirected edges, for every \(T_0\) and every common strictly positive terminal selection kernel. Its contrapositive is a necessary condition for recovery on that subclass, and at \(T_0=V\) the result is an equivalence with executable EXT-ID success for every ordinarily identifiable positive-model cell. The algebraic model class, the soundness theorem for successful EXT-ID outputs, and the fixed-fiber response characterization remain valid beyond this subclass under their own premises. No claim is made that arbitrary EXT-ID failure implies a feasible response witness, that QE3 has been run, or that universal completeness has been established. The response slack in the transfer is witness-specific after zero labels are removed. Qiu et al. are treated only as an input-shape and scalar-estimand analogue. The ACTG 320 extension using WIHS or CNICS margins is a downstream audit consumer, not validation of the theorem.

project_justification.gap: Ordinary ID completeness gives graph obstructions from a full observational law, and Kivva et al. restore positive-model witnesses for positive general identification. Neither result by itself proves that a positive same-\(P(V)\) witness pair remains observationally indistinguishable after conditioning on selection while also matching an unbiased external margin. Correa et al. provide sound recovery for the selected-law-plus-margin problem without a completeness theorem; do-search likewise has no negative-answer guarantee for unrestricted generalized-identifiability inputs of this shape. Qiu et al. are an input-shape and scalar-ATE analogue under probability-class assumptions, not a literal intersection with the present arbitrary finite ADMG class.
project_justification.niche: The tractable missing step is a graph-native transfer on diagrams where selection is a terminal sink with no incident bidirected edge: determine what ordinary positive-model nonidentification implies for the normalized selected conditional plus an arbitrary population margin, without assuming a representation-specific null vector.
project_justification.fill: The new theorem lifts the positive substantive witness pair through any common strictly positive terminal selection kernel, derives a common selected conditional and every \(T_0\)-margin, proves exact positive-fiber membership and retained causal separation, and obtains a common witness-specific response slack by finite response reduction. Its contrapositive is a necessary condition for two-law recovery on this subclass. At \(T_0=V\), initialization and ordinary do-calculus completeness give the reverse implication and executable EXT-ID success, yielding the exact equivalence. This is a scoped structural identification result; it does not establish arbitrary-failure completeness for EXT-ID.

thm:projective-nullspace-certificate.justification: This is a supporting fixed-representation certificate: once a query row escapes the normalized selected-law and margin row space, an explicit interior perturbation yields an exact same-input pair.
thm:projective-nullspace-certificate.gap: Its normalized cross-product constraints are specific to the two-law fiber, but it is conditional and is not the graph-level headline.
thm:projective-nullspace-certificate.consumer: It supports explicit response-fiber witnesses and the named three-node diagnostic; it is not used to infer that every EXT-ID failure is feasible.

thm:three-node-interior-witness.justification: The four-response-type construction is an exact rational stress test and a fully interior nonidentification certificate for the named graph.
thm:three-node-interior-witness.gap: It preserves both a uniform selected conditional and a uniform external margin while moving the intervention cell from \(3/8\) to \(5/8\).
thm:three-node-interior-witness.consumer: It is the certified first kill-test instance; it is not evidence that the remaining three-node census has been executed.

thm:positive-ordinary-hedge-selection-li.justification: This theorem gives a graph-native lift from ordinary positive-model nonidentification to exact two-law nonidentification without a representation-specific row-separation premise.
thm:positive-ordinary-hedge-selection-li.gap: The cited result supplies a positive same-\(P(V)\) pair; the new calculation preserves the normalized selected conditional, every external margin, causal separation, and common witness-specific response slack.
thm:positive-ordinary-hedge-selection-li.consumer: Its contrapositive is the necessary condition for recovery on terminal selection sinks without incident bidirected edges.

thm:canonical-response-fiber-characteriz.justification: This replaces an unsupported universal failure theorem with an exact finite witness criterion whose variables and constraints are explicit.
thm:canonical-response-fiber-characteriz.gap: The formula simultaneously enforces graph compatibility, positive supports, two positive selection normalizers, normalized selected-law cross-products, exact margin rows, and unequal causal cells.
thm:canonical-response-fiber-characteriz.consumer: A feasible response pair is a directly checkable exact-fiber nonrecoverability certificate for a proposed external margin.

prop:boundary-reductions.justification: At \(T_0=V\), initialization exposes the full population law and supplies the achievability half of the ordinary-ID equivalence.
prop:boundary-reductions.gap: This is an executable boundary reduction, not a completeness result for arbitrary external margins.
prop:boundary-reductions.consumer: Combined with the terminal-selection necessity proposition, it gives the exact full-margin equivalence and success audit.

thm:extid-sound-termination.justification: This theorem certifies every returned arithmetic expression and finite termination, independently of the scoped necessity result.
thm:extid-sound-termination.gap: It deliberately makes no claim that \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) is a universal nonidentification certificate.
thm:extid-sound-termination.consumer: It validates successful ACTG audit formulas and, at \(T_0=V\), the ordinary-ID replay supplied by the boundary proposition.

prop:terminal-selection-ordinary-id-nece.justification: This is the headline graph-level recovery restriction, with an exact ordinary-ID equivalence when the external margin is the full population law.
prop:terminal-selection-ordinary-id-nece.gap: Ordinary ID completeness alone does not establish preservation of both observed sources under selection; the selection-lift theorem supplies that missing direction.
prop:terminal-selection-ordinary-id-nece.consumer: It gives the structural audit rule for terminal-unconfounded ACTG selection diagrams and the full-margin EXT-ID success boundary.

sampling_model.treatment: Each decision run fixes one intervention-outcome cell \((x,y)\). The general algebraic procedure permits any finite selection ADMG \(\mathcal G\); the graph-level transfer and ordinary-ID comparison additionally require that \(S\) be terminal and have no incident bidirected edge.
